commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Done. `server/mcp/mcp-http-handler.ts` reports **0 errors**, and a before/after diff of the full `tsc` output shows **only deletions** — the 20 target errors vanished and no error appeared in any other file.

## What was actually wrong

Every error traced to the same anti-pattern: values were cast through `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>`, which erases real types and degrades every field read off them to `unknown`/`{}`. The fix was to delete those casts and give the values their real types.

**The Zod→JSON Schema converter (14 of the 20 errors).** Zod 4 *does* type `_def` — `_def.entries`, `_def.element`, `_def.innerType`, `_def.defaultValue`, and `isOptional()` are all properly typed once you stop casting the schema away. Rewriting the converter around `instanceof` narrowing plus the real `_def` types resolved all of them, and gave the function a declared `JsonSchemaNode` return type instead of `any`.

Two things surfaced while typing it:
- **The array branch was passing the wrong value.** It read `_def.type`, which in Zod 4 is the discriminator string `'array'`, not the element schema. Array item schemas were never being converted. Now uses `_def.element`.
- **Two `_def.typeName === 'ZodEnum' / 'ZodNativeEnum'` branches were Zod-3 leftovers**, unreachable under Zod 4 (`typeName` doesn't exist on `$ZodTypeDef`, which is why they errored). Zod 4 represents both `z.enum` and `z.nativeEnum` as `ZodEnum`, so they're consolidated into the single `instanceof z.ZodEnum` branch — same reachable behavior, one code path.

**The two call sites** now use an `isZodSchema()` type guard instead of duck-typing through a cast, which is what makes the mixed catalog (hand-written JSON Schema literals + real Zod instances) type correctly at the branch.

**The transport boundary (6 errors).** `params.arguments` and the auth fields on `req` got named types — `JsonRpcToolCallParams` and `AuthenticatedMcpRequest` (following `mcp-auth`'s existing `Request & { apiKey?: string }` idiom). Reads of untyped argument values are coerced at the point of use (`asNonEmptyString`, a `typeof === 'number'` check for `thresholdMinutes`) rather than asserted, preserving the original `||` fallback semantics.

One deliberate behavior note: typing `params.name` as `string | undefined` exposed that the bridge fallback could pass `undefined` as a tool name. I made that `''`, which the bridge reports as an unknown tool — previously it would have passed `undefined` into a lookup. Neither is a working call; the typed version just fails legibly.

I left the changes uncommitted in the working tree.
